result.summary: This pull request integrates Bitcoin Core's hardware-accelerated SHA256 transform into libsecp256k1 contexts using the external compression hook introduced in upstream libsecp256k1 #1777. It restructures `ECC_Context` into a proper singleton managing both signing and verification contexts, moves ECC initialization into `common/ecc_init`, and updates all call sites across binaries, tests, and benchmarks.
result.problem: Libsecp256k1 previously relied solely on its internal software SHA256 implementation, leaving hardware acceleration (ARM SHA-NI, x86 SHA-NI) unused during signing and verification. Furthermore, ECC context initialization was coupled to key primitives rather than managed through a unified lifecycle.

categories.rationale: Signing speeds improve significantly on CPUs with SHA extensions (ECDSASign is 13% faster and SchnorrSign is 7% faster on ARM64), though verification performance is largely unaffected. It also delivers clean RAII lifecycle management for secp256k1 contexts, though the improvement is not blocking any critical safety issues.

result.card: PR #36188 plugs Bitcoin Core's hardware-accelerated SHA256 compression function into libsecp256k1 contexts and encapsulates ECC context initialization into a unified RAII singleton. This improves ECDSA signing performance by roughly 13% and Schnorr signing by 7% on architectures with hardware SHA extensions, while verification performance remains essentially flat. The changes clean up global ECC state handling across bitcoind and auxiliary tools without blocking critical projects. Review state is fully ready, having earned unanimous Concept ACKs from six maintainers and contributors with detailed code review still to follow.
